note: Two ways to make this pack. The committed MP3s were generated by the `kokoro` block with the bf_emma voice (British English), the closest available fallback because Kokoro-82M ships no Australian voice. The top-level model/voice/instructions drive only the optional OpenAI path (`npm run narration:generate:openai`) and are kept aligned with the accent of the committed pack.
instructions: Speak in a natural British English accent, like a warm, unhurried parent guiding one curious five-year-old. Calm, natural and friendly, never announcer-like or sing-song. Use short pauses between ideas, clear consonants, and a gently excited tone. Do not rush. Do not add words that are not in the script.

cues.arrival-earth: We made it to Earth! This is our home, seen from space.
cues.find-earth: Now, can you find the three gold places? Tap each one you see.
cues.arrival-moon: We made it to the Moon! There is no air or weather here.
cues.find-moon: Now, can you find the three gold places? Tap each one you see.
cues.arrival-mars: We made it to Mars! Its red dust is full of rust.
cues.find-mars: Now, can you find the three gold places? Tap each one you see.
cues.discovery-earth-sahara: You found the Sahara! It is the biggest hot desert in the world, and it is enormous even from space.
cues.discovery-earth-amazon: You found the Amazon rainforest! More kinds of animals live here than anywhere else on Earth.
cues.discovery-earth-nightside: You found Earth's night side! Those tiny glows are towns and cities full of people.
cues.discovery-moon-tranquility: You found the Apollo 11 landing place! The astronauts' footprints are still there because there is no wind or rain.
cues.discovery-moon-tycho: You found Tycho! A crashing space rock splashed those bright streaks of dust across the Moon.
cues.discovery-moon-farside: You found the Moon's far side! People never saw this side until a spacecraft flew around it.
cues.discovery-mars-olympus: You found Olympus Mons! It is the biggest volcano in the whole solar system.
cues.discovery-mars-marineris: You found Valles Marineris! This giant crack is longer than Australia is wide.
cues.discovery-mars-elysium: You found Elysium Mons! This volcano would still be twice as tall as Earth's tallest mountain.
cues.hunt-earth: One more is hiding. Swipe the planet sideways to look around the back.
cues.hunt-moon: One more is hiding. Swipe the Moon sideways to look around the back.
cues.hunt-mars: One more is hiding. Swipe Mars sideways to look around the back.
cues.success-earth: You found all three places on Earth!
cues.success-moon: You found all three places on the Moon!
cues.success-mars: You found all three places on Mars!
cues.spin-earth: Watch the sunlight move while Earth turns. The bright side is day, and the dark side is night.
cues.discovery-earth-lakes: You found the Great Lakes! Five huge lakes joined together, holding more fresh water than almost anywhere on Earth.
cues.discovery-earth-himalaya: You found the Himalayas! The tallest mountains on Earth are down there, and they are still getting taller.
cues.discovery-earth-reef: You found the Great Barrier Reef! It is the biggest reef in the world, and tiny animals built every bit of it.
cues.spin-moon: Watch day come to the Moon. Its days are very long: two weeks of sunshine, then two weeks of dark.
cues.discovery-moon-procellarum: You found the Ocean of Storms! There is no water in it at all. It is a huge flat plain of old cooled rock.
cues.discovery-moon-crisium: You found the Sea of Crises! A gigantic rock smashed in here, and melted rock filled the hole right up.
cues.discovery-moon-orientale: You found Orientale! It really is shaped like a bullseye, with rings of mountains inside rings of mountains.
cues.spin-mars: Watch day come to Mars. A day here is almost exactly as long as a day on Earth.
cues.discovery-mars-hellas: You found Hellas! It is a hole so deep that Earth's biggest mountain would fit right inside it.
cues.discovery-mars-jezero: You found Jezero crater! A robot landed here with a tiny helicopter, the first one ever to fly on another world.
cues.discovery-mars-gale: You found Gale crater! A robot the size of a car has been driving around down here, drilling into the rocks.
cues.spin-saturn: Watch day come to Saturn. It spins so fast that a whole day here is only about ten hours long.
cues.arrival-saturn: We made it to Saturn! This is the planet with the beautiful rings.
cues.find-saturn: Now, can you find the three gold places? Tap each one you see.
cues.discovery-saturn-rings: You found the rings! They are billions of pieces of ice and rock going round Saturn, from tiny crumbs to lumps as big as a house.
cues.discovery-saturn-hexagon: You found the six-sided storm! Right at the top of Saturn is a giant cloud shaped like a hexagon, with six straight sides.
cues.discovery-saturn-storm: You found a giant storm! Saturn's storms are far bigger than any on Earth, and they can rumble on for months.
cues.hunt-saturn: One more is hiding. Swipe Saturn sideways to look around the back.
cues.success-saturn: You found all three! You have been all the way out to Saturn.
cues.discovery-saturn-division: You found the big gap in the rings! One of Saturn's moons keeps sweeping it clear, over and over.
cues.discovery-saturn-jet: You found Saturn's fastest wind! Round the middle it never stops blowing, quicker than a jet plane.
cues.discovery-saturn-bands: You found the stripes! Each stripe is a band of cloud, and every one races round Saturn at its own speed.
